newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Verdicts in Bahrain trial of 81 expected this month.
newsitem.headline: Verdicts in Bahrain trial of 81 expected this month.

text.p: The trial of 81 people accused of involvement in an alleged Iranian-backed plot to topple Bahrain's government entered its third day on Monday, with verdicts expected this month.

Lawyers said of 81 people accused of taking part, 59 are appearing in court while the rest remain at large and are being tried in absentia. The 59 suspects have been divided into seven groups. The first group went to court on Saturday.

"The State Security Court is trying a third group today at Bahrain's coast guard station," a defence lawyer told Reuters. "The court's verdicts are expected to be passed before the end of this month."

The defendants are accused of joining the military wing of the Bahraini Hizbollah (Party of God), creating an organisation aimed at toppling the government, possessing weapons without permission and contacting a foreign country.
Political parties are banned in Bahrain.
The lawyers said the suspects could face the death penalty if convicted.
Bahrain in June accused Shi'ite Moslem Iran of backing an attempt to topple the government and said it had arrested around 60 people in connection with the alleged plot.

Iran denied interfering in the internal affairs of Bahrain, where members of the island's majority Shi'ite Moslem community demanding political and economic reform by the Sunni rulers have waged a campaign of bombings, arson attacks, sabotage and riots since December 1994.
At least 28 people have been killed and hundreds arrested in more than two years of unrest.
